nowhere adverb

also not anywhere, nowhere else, nowhere to be found, nowhere on earth, go nowhere, not going anywhere

classical

Ter. Ad. 4.2.1: frātrem nusquam inveniō gentium (Lewis & Short)

Traupman 352

nusquam

adverb

nowhere, in no place; to no place

Both “in no place” and, with verbs of motion, “to no place”: nusquam abeō, “I’m not going anywhere” (Ter. Ad. 2.2.38). nusquam gentium is “nowhere on earth”, nusquam alibī “nowhere else”, nusquam nōn “everywhere”. It also means “on no occasion, in nothing”.

Other words

  • nūllibī — nowhere

    adverb · avoid · post-classical · Vitr. 7.1.4, doubtful reading (Lewis & Short)

    Late and rare; the word is nusquam.

Examples

  • nusquam hercle equidem illam videō

    I can’t see her anywhere, by HerculesPlaut. Rud. 465–470

  • nusquam est quī ubīque est

    whoever is everywhere is nowhereSen. Ep. 2.2

  • potes apparātius cēnāre apud multōs, nusquam hilarius simplicius incautius

    you can dine more grandly at many houses, but nowhere more merrily, simply and freelyPlin. Ep. 1.15.4

See also everywhere, somewhere, else, appear, disappear.

SourcesLewis & Short: nusquam · Lewis & Short: nullibi

Plautus, Seneca and Pliny from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-plautus, loci-seneca-epistulae, loci-plinius); Terence and Cicero as Lewis & Short quotes them.

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 352.
